title: log_read leaks the full command-array allocation on every corrupt/truncated/unknown-tag log
evidence:
cmds = make([]Command, n, allocator)
	for i in 0 ..< int(n) {
		cmd: Command
		cmd.apply_tick = r_u64(&r)
		switch r_u8(&r) {
...
		case 7:
			cmd.kind = Cmd_Place_Router{type_idx = r_u16(&r), pos = {r_i32(&r), r_i32(&r)}}
		case:
			return {}, nil, false
		}
		cmds[i] = cmd
	}
	if r.bad || r.pos != len(r.data) { return {}, nil, false } // truncation/trailing = corrupt
	return h, cmds, true
--- harness/replay.odin:70:
	header, cmds, ok := pp.log_read(data, context.allocator)
detail: Every failure return after `make` (unknown tag, truncation, trailing bytes) drops the record array; the caller receives nil and cannot free the heap allocation, which is proportional to the log length. A crafted replay file turns input size into unrecoverable memory.
recommended_fix: delete(cmds) before each post-allocation `return {}, nil, false`, or parse into context.temp_allocator so the harness's per-tick free_all reclaims it.

title: Grant/starting-inventory counts accept negative and Float-typed values — a negative grant drives tray stock negative and locks that tier for the run
detail: The loader's own contract says out-of-range values abort with a named error, but grant/starting counts are only type-checked: a negative n is applied raw by `+= it.n`, silently corrupting the tray invariant and soft-locking that tier's draws for the rest of the run.
recommended_fix: Reject n <= 0 (and json.Float) in starting_inventory and grants with a named Catalog_Error, mirroring the unknown-tier checks two lines below.

title: Catalog loader leaks heap allocations on success (jarr_i color/weight arrays never freed) and orphans partial Catalogs on every error path
detail: jarr_i allocates on the load allocator and no caller deletes it: one leaked array per packet_type (color) plus two per load (jw3 presets); every must_catalogs() test call leaks, and the new(Catalogs) plus partial arrays are orphaned whenever catalogs_load returns an error.
recommended_fix: defer delete(c) in the color path and free jarr_i's out buffer in jw3; delete the partial catalogs before each error return in catalogs_load.
